title: Relative surplus-value via higher productivity
claim: Surplus-value can be raised without lengthening the day by cutting necessary labour-time, which requires cheapening the goods that enter workers' subsistence and thus revolutionising the technical and social mode of production.
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Largely a definitional/analytical decomposition of the working day; the labour-theory framework makes it hard to falsify as stated.
notes: Individual capitalists do not aim at lowering labour-power's value; it is the aggregate result (ch12-p009).

title: Co-operation: social power appropriated by capital
claim: Productive power arising from many labourers working together costs capital nothing and appears as a natural power of capital, because workers are isolated sellers until the labour-process begins, when they become 'modes of existence of capital'.
quote: it appears as a power with which capital is endowed by Nature
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Interpretive claim about who the surplus from collective productivity accrues to; hard to falsify, though distribution of gains from scale is empirically discussable.

title: Manufacture and the detail labourer
claim: Manufacture, resting on handicraft skill, splits crafts into fractional operations, producing a collective labourer ('a productive mechanism whose parts are human beings') more productive but made up of crippled detail workers, as a method of generating relative surplus-value.
quote: a productive mechanism whose parts are human beings
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Claims about productivity gains and worker deskilling/narrowing under division of labour can be compared with later evidence.

title: Anarchy of market vs despotism of workshop
claim: Division of labour in society is coordinated only ex post through commodity exchange and competition, while inside the workshop it is planned under the capitalist's undisputed authority; the two are mutually conditioning. Bourgeois thought praises the latter and condemns planning of the former.
quote: anarchy in the social division of labour and despotism in that of the workshop
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Structural characterisation; 'authority in workshop and society in inverse ratio' is stylised and not cleanly falsifiable.
notes: Marx cites his own Misere (fn36). Also states workshop division is special to capitalism (ch14-p039).

title: Machinery system as objective automaton
claim: Machinery replaces the subjective principle of division of labour with an objective analysis of the process into phases handled by a chain of machines driven by a central automaton; continuity becomes imperative and the worker becomes an appendage to the system.
quote: the labourer becomes a mere appendage to an already existing material condition of production
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Whether automation systems subordinate worker pacing and make labour an appendage can be compared with later factory/automation history.
notes: Marx notes the tool, not labour, is the starting point of machines (ch15-p004, fn15).

title: Value transfer and the limits of machinery use
claim: Machines create no new value but pass on their own value piecemeal; they are productive only if they cost less labour than they displace, and for the capitalist only if they cost less than the wages (value of labour-power) they replace.
quote: The productiveness of a machine is therefore measured by the human labour-power it replaces.
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Rests on the labour theory of value; the capitalist's cost-comparison part is separately captured in another item.

title: Immanent drive to raise productivity and cheapen the worker
claim: Capital has a constant tendency to raise productivity so as to cheapen commodities and, through cheaper necessaries, to cheapen the labourer himself (lower the value of labour-power), enlarging relative surplus-value.
quote: an inclination and constant tendency, to heighten the productiveness of labour
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Testable as: sustained productivity growth, falling real cost of wage goods, and a rising share of the day/output going to profit; wage share data can contradict or support it.
notes: Also answers Quesnay's riddle why the capitalist lowers exchange-value (ch12-p014). The 'cheapens the labourer' step presumes wages track the value of necessaries.

title: Productivity gains are not used to shorten the working day
claim: Increased productiveness under capitalism aims at shortening the labour-time per commodity, not at shortening the worker's day; the worker can produce ten times as much and still work 12 or even 14 hours.
quote: The shortening of the working day is, therefore, by no means what is aimed at
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Compare long-run trends in hours of work against productivity growth, controlling for legislation and union struggle.
notes: Marx's broader text credits legislation/struggle for limits; ch12 only claims capital by itself has no such aim.

title: Competition forces diffusion of new methods; extra profit is transient
claim: The innovating capitalist earns extra surplus-value because his individual value is below social value, but this vanishes once the method becomes general; the law of value acts as a coercive law of competition compelling rivals to adopt it.
quote: this extra surplus-value vanishes, so soon as the new method of production has become general
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Predicts innovation rents erode with diffusion and that competitive pressure drives technology adoption; observable in industry studies (though patents/monopoly can slow erosion).
notes: Marx explicitly postpones full analysis of competition (ch12-p010).

title: Rising minimum capital and concentration of means of production
claim: As division of labour and scale advance, the minimum capital each capitalist must hold must keep increasing, so social means of production and subsistence are ever more transformed into capital in fewer hands; co-operation's scale depends on this concentration.
quote: it is a law, based on the very nature of manufacture
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Testable as rising minimum efficient scale / capital intensity and concentration of ownership over time; contested by small-firm and service-sector evidence.
notes: Quote is from ch14-p040: 'a law, based on the very nature of manufacture, that the minimum amount of capital... must keep increasing'. Stated for manufacture; generalisation to later capitalism is Marx's wider claim.

title: Supervision becomes a specialised, hierarchical wage-function and a site of conflict
claim: As co-operation grows, capital delegates supervision to a class of managers and foremen who command in the capitalist's name; control is both a technical coordination function and an instrument of exploitation, and resistance grows with the number of workers.
quote: As the number of the co-operating labourers increases, so too does their resistance
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Predicts growth of a managerial/supervisory stratum and persistent labour-management conflict; the claim that managerial control is 'identical' with exploitative control is partly interpretive.
notes: Also claims capitalist's power descends from Oriental despots, 'whether he be an isolated, or as in joint-stock companies, a collective capitalist' (ch13-p024). Opponent view that leadership is merely technical: ch13-p020.

title: Manufacture deskills: unskilled class, hierarchy, falling value of labour-power
claim: Detail labour creates a hierarchy of labour-powers and a new class of 'unskilled' workers; apprenticeship costs fall so the value of labour-power falls, raising surplus-value, except where decomposition creates new comprehensive functions.
quote: Manufacture begets, in every handicraft that it seizes upon, a class of so-called unskilled labourers
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Deskilling hypotheses can be tested against occupational wage and skill data; Marx himself notes an exception for new skilled functions.
notes: In the manufacturing period itself, unskilled numbers stayed limited because skilled workers resisted (ch14-p056).

title: Separation of intellect from manual labour completed by science serving capital
claim: The separation of the knowledge and judgement of production from the labourer begins in co-operation, develops in manufacture and is completed in modern industry, which makes science a productive force distinct from labour and enlists it in capital's service; each worker is impoverished as capital is enriched in social productive power.
quote: It is completed in modern industry, which makes science a productive force distinct from labour
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Can be checked against trends in task fragmentation, scientific management, and R&D concentrated in firms vs. worker autonomy; evidence on upskilling vs deskilling is mixed.
notes: Quote of exactly the first 15 words; see ch14-p042. Marx quotes Thompson, Ferguson, Smith as sources (fn44, 43, 45).

title: Division of labour damages workers' bodies and minds
claim: Manufacture, by attacking the individual at the root of his life, is the first to supply material for industrial pathology; the detail labourer is stunted physically (curvature, muscle deformity) and mentally, and some employers preferred half-idiotic workers for secret operations.
quote: What is lost by the detail labourers, is concentrated in the capital that employs them.
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Occupational health and cognitive effects of repetitive work are empirically studied; the cognitive-stunting claim is largely borrowed from Smith and Ferguson.
notes: Smith and Ferguson and Urquhart voice the strongest statements (speaker for those quotes is source:Smith/Ferguson/Urquhart).

title: Insubordination of skilled labour is capital's problem until machinery
claim: Because handicraft skill is the foundation of manufacture and the mechanism has no framework apart from workers, capital must constantly wrestle with insubordination and complaints of indiscipline; machines, made by the manufacturing machine-shop, remove the technical reason for tying workers to a detail and loosen the fetters on capital.
quote: capital is constantly compelled to wrestle with the insubordination of the workmen
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Testable via historical labour-discipline evidence; plausible but the claim that machinery solved the problem is contestable (machine-paced work also generates resistance).
notes: Ure's and the 1770 author's remarks serve as evidence (source/opponent).

title: One technical revolution forces revolutions in connected industries and transport
claim: A radical change in one branch (spinning) makes change in dependent branches (weaving, bleaching, dyeing, ginning) imperative and revolutionises communication and transport (steamers, railways, telegraph); in turn modern industry must build machines by machines to stand on its own technical foundation.
quote: A radical change in the mode of production in one sphere of industry
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Cross-sector technological complementarity and the rise of machine-tool industries are well-studied; the strong necessity claim is testable against counter-cases.
notes: Steam power concentrated production in towns (ch15-p011, quoting inspector Redgrave: 'steam-engine is the parent of manufacturing towns').

title: Machinery enrols women and children and dilutes the family wage
claim: Machinery makes muscular strength unnecessary, so capital first seeks women and children; the value of the male worker's labour-power is spread over the whole family, depreciating it, so the family must supply more surplus-labour to live, and the degree of exploitation rises.
quote: It thus depreciates his labour-power.
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Predicts rising family labour-force participation without proportional rise in household income; compare with later household-earner data (the later shift to dual-earner households).
notes: Marx says the cost of keeping the family rises as home production is replaced by purchases (fn39). Contested later by the 'family wage' ideal.

title: Machinery breaks male workers' resistance
claim: By adding women and children to the ranks, machinery overcomes the resistance that male operatives in the manufacturing period offered to capital's despotism; they become docile and compelled to exert themselves.
quote: machinery at last breaks down the resistance which the male operatives
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Compare strike/bargaining outcomes after mechanisation and female labour entry; evidence is mixed since later unions organised factory labour.
notes: Evidence in fn60 is Lord Ashley quoting a manufacturer (source).

title: Machine adoption depends on the wage level, not on labour saved
claim: The capitalist's limit to using a machine is the gap between machine price and the wage bill it replaces, not the labour saved; so machines are invented in dear-labour countries and not used where wages sit below the value of labour-power (surplus population), while labour legislation can spur machinery.
quote: Hence nowhere do we find a more shameful squandering of human labour-power
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: A testable 'induced innovation / factor price' hypothesis: high wages and labour restrictions raise mechanisation, cheap labour retards it (e.g. US vs UK, post-regulation substitution).
notes: Fn33 asserts a communist society would use machines differently; Ricardo agrees machinery is often unusable until wages rise (fn36).

title: Capital levels conditions: limits on child labour spread across industries
claim: Because capital is a leveller demanding equal conditions of exploitation in every sphere, a legal limit on child labour in one branch becomes the cause of its limitation in others; the state intervenes because machinery undermines the free-contract appearance.
quote: since capital is by nature a leveller
speaker: marx
testable_rationale: Predicts regulatory diffusion across sectors and competitive pressure for uniform labour standards; compare with regulatory spillover and avoidance (e.g. shift to unregulated sectors).
notes: The manufacturers' counter-claim that children are moved to unregulated trades is also noted (ch15-p042).

title: Mill: machinery has not lightened anyone's toil
claim: J. S. Mill's remark that it is doubtful all mechanical inventions have lightened any human being's daily toil. Marx treats it as true in effect but beside the point, since lightening toil is not capital's aim.
quote: It is questionable if all the mechanical inventions yet made have lightened the day's toil
speaker: opponent:Mill
testable_rationale: Hours/toil trends are testable.
notes: Marx partly agrees (fn1: true except for the idle fed by others' labour); not a straightforward opponent claim he refutes.

title: MacCulloch/Ure/Senior: gratitude to capital for productivity
claim: Economists say on one page that workers owe thanks to capital for shortening necessary labour-time, and on the next that they must repay by working 15 hours instead of 10. Marx cites this as an example of apologetic inconsistency.
speaker: opponent:MacCulloch/Ure/Senior
testable_rationale: Marx's paraphrase of economists' attitude, not a quoted claim.
notes: Marx gives no direct citation here; unclear whether he is paraphrasing or characterising; treat as caricature.

title: Garnier: state education of the masses violates division of labour
claim: Garnier, opposing A. Smith's mild proposal for public education, argued that mixing hand-work and head-work classes would proscribe the whole social system and that government should not hinder the natural course of division of labour.
quote: our whole social system would be proscribed.
speaker: opponent:Garnier
testable_rationale: Can be compared with the later expansion of mass education and its effect on economic growth.
notes: Marx also records Smith's contrary recommendation and Ferguson's warnings (ch14-p046-p049).

title: Ure: skill breeds intractability; Arkwright created order
claim: Ure says skilful workers become self-willed and unfit components of a mechanical system, and that Arkwright's factory 'created order' where manufacture based on division of labour lacked it. Marx quotes this as evidence of capital's discipline problem.
quote: Arkwright created order.
speaker: opponent:Ure
testable_rationale: Whether machine systems reduced indiscipline and need for skilled labour is checkable historically.
notes: Marx uses Ure as an apologist whose admissions support Marx's own point; treat as source/opponent hybrid.

title: Ricardo/Say: machines add no value or render value-creating service
claim: Ricardo treats machines like gratuitous natural agents that add nothing to value (Marx says this is right only against Say's view that machines render value-creating 'service' forming part of profits), but sometimes loses sight of the value machines transfer.
quote: as they perform their work gratuitously, the assistance which they afford us, adds nothing
speaker: opponent:Say
testable: A dispute within value theory, not an empirical claim about the future.
testable_rationale: Say's 'service' claim is opposed; Ricardo is partly agreed with and partly criticised (fn24). Interest on machines is deferred to Book III (fn26).
